name: ArangoDB
tagline: Native multi-model database: documents, graphs, search and vectors behind one query language.
description: ArangoDB stores JSON documents and lets you treat collections as graph vertices and edges, so document queries, joins, graph traversals and full-text search (ArangoSearch) share one query language, AQL. It runs as a single server or as a sharded cluster with SmartGraphs for locality. Recent 3.12 releases added a vector index aimed at GraphRAG. The company now markets itself as Arango (arango.ai). Since 3.12 the source is BSL 1.1, and the free Community binaries carry a 100 GiB production dataset limit and a ban on commercial production use, which changes the calculus for many teams. ArangoDB 4.0 is still in development.

license.name: Business Source License 1.1; ArangoDB Community License for binaries

pricing.notes: Community binaries are free for non-commercial production up to 100 GiB; Enterprise subscriptions and the Arango Managed Platform (ex-ArangoGraph) for everything else.

scale.notes: Cluster mode shards collections across DB-Servers; SmartGraphs and OneShard reduce network hops. Cross-datacenter replication was dropped in 3.12.

strengths: One query language (AQL) for documents, joins, graph traversals and search
ArangoSearch provides ranked full-text and hybrid search without Elasticsearch
Graphs are just document collections, so no separate graph store to sync
SmartGraphs and OneShard deployments for low-latency clustered graph queries
Kubernetes operator and managed cloud offering
weaknesses: BSL plus the Community License's 100 GiB / non-commercial limits make the free edition unsuitable for most businesses
Cluster transactions are not fully ACID across shards
Smaller ecosystem than Neo4j for graphs or MongoDB for documents
No built-in cross-region replication in current releases
useCases: Fraud and network analysis mixed with document data
notIdealFor: Startups wanting a free production database over 100 GiB
